content.text:
Here’s How Global Bond Managers Are Playing Higher Yields
America’s Treasury troubles are prompting bond investors to diversify their portfolios.
You might still be on vacation mode, but world leaders aren’t. Over the past week, trade negotiations between the U.S. and Canada broke down; U.K.-Russia tensions mounted after U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham reaffirmed his support for Ukraine; and the U.S. unveiled new sanctions on Iran in what President Donald Trump called an “Economic D-Day.” We’ll get to Iran later in this issue, but first, I’m taking a look at another topic that is causing quite an uproar: the bond market. Recent fluctuations in long-duration bonds are shaking up the way global bond managers are thinking about capital allocations. And in a bid to better understand why U.S.-Canada talks fell apart this weekend, I chatted with Wilbur Ross, former secretary of commerce in the first Trump administration. Mentioned in this newsletter: Treasuries, Scott Bessent, Donald Trump, Meta Platforms, Wilbur Ross, Mark Carney, USMCA, Greenland, SK Telecom, Xi Jinping. You can subscribe to Barron’s Global Signals here.
